+import json

pull_requests.body:
Closes #758

- `anton-oss` (values-oss.yaml) gets the `anton` twin's dind sidecar: same `docker:dind` image and dockerd args (mirror.gcr.io), `DOCKER_HOST` and `RUNNER_WAIT_FOR_DOCKER_IN_SECONDS` on the runner. Volumes are emptyDir only; no BuildKit client certificate, no host mount, host network or secret.
- `anton-oss-light` and `anton-oss-batch` stay daemon-free.
- `test_isolation.py`: every set keeps no token, no service links, no host network/PID/IPC, emptyDir-only volumes, no secret env, unprivileged runner; only the standard set runs a dind sidecar, matching its twin's image and args.

Red proof: the test commit alone on `diffcheck/ci-323133-0320-red` (run 38302930098) must fail on the standard set's missing daemon.

Hazard: dind is privileged. Routing to `anton-oss` stays behind the trusted actor runs-on expression; fork PR workflows on agentihooks and agentibrain-kernel need approval for all external contributors. Rollback: `git revert` of this commit.

Red proof: the test commit alone on `diffcheck/ci-323133-0320-red` (run 38302930098) must fail on the standard set's missing daemon.

Hazard: dind is privileged. Routing to `anton-oss` stays behind the trusted actor runs-on expression; fork PR workflows on agentihooks and agentibrain-kernel need approval for all external contributors. Rollback: `git revert` of this commit.

before_state.pull_request_title: Run the swarm ledger hook on every harness through the shared hooks entry, with a wiring parity test
before_state.pull_request_body:
Closes #2999

The swarm ledger hook (`scripts/swarm_ledger/ledger_hook.py`) was wired only in the Claude settings base. Codex and Copilot never ran it, so on those harnesses `ledger join` never bound the session, operator events were never shown, the acknowledge stop block never fired, and the ledger server never autostarted.

## Audit (dev at c60db3fdc)
| Event | Claude | Codex | Copilot |
|---|---|---|---|
| SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop | shared hooks + ledger hook | shared hooks | shared hooks |
| SessionEnd, PreToolUse, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, PermissionRequest | shared hooks | shared hooks | shared hooks |
| Notification | shared hooks | none (Codex has no such event) | shared hooks |

## Change
- `hooks.context.swarm_ledger.run` runs `ledger_hook.dispatch` in-process. It returns the hook's context blocks and its stop reason.
- `hook_manager` calls it on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse, and on Stop after the turn's own stop work but before refresh and close scheduling. Context goes through `inject_context`; the stop hold is raised as `BlockAction`.
- The Claude-only ledger hook entries are removed from `profiles/_base/settings.base.json`.
- `join_from_new` also reads Copilot's `textResultForLlm`.
- `tests/test_hook_parity.py` builds each harness's hook wiring from the real adapters and fails when a hook is wired for one harness and not the others, or bypasses the shared entry. Named differences:
  - `UNSUPPORTED`: Codex has no Notification event.
  - `UNHELD`: Copilot `agentStop` has no block channel. This is tied to `_COPILOT_BLOCKABLE_EVENTS`.

## Evidence
- Red: Proofs run 38331551961 on 5c84c9b83 failed. The parity tests failed on the ledger hook wiring, and the shared-entry module was absent.
- Green: Proofs run 38334090815 on 0b1495348: 4748 passed, 354 skipped. It covered the parity, shared entry, hook manager, hook targets, swarm ledger, Codex, Copilot, conditions and inbox suites.
- Mutation preflight run 38334090419 on 0b1495348 passed.
- Review: Standards and Spec readers closed after three rounds. Accepted residuals, by ruling:
  - The ledger's former 10 s per-process timeout is gone. The shared entry already runs uncapped reads on the same events.
  - A held stop still clears per-turn signals and sets the heartbeat to idle, as the old Claude path did.

before_state.task: A ledger event without a revision is refused when written and never stops the metrics pass
before_state.task_text: Parent: swarm runtime fixes keep one bad record from stopping a whole pass. The metrics pass reads each stored ledger event revision strictly, so one event without a revision would stop every metrics pass and its acknowledgement.
